title: HTTP endpoints
summary: A route attribute on a request becomes a real ASP.NET endpoint, generated at build time. The request is bound from the body with route and query values applied over it, and a failed result becomes a problem response. Endpoints require an authenticated caller unless they say otherwise, a body must declare a JSON media type, and both the reading and the writing are replaceable seams.
useWhen: Commands and queries need to be reachable over HTTP. Do not write controllers, minimal-API mapping code, or your own result-to-status-code mapping; implement IResponseWriter instead of forking the package when the envelope has to be your own.
